baseline: The page claims that a model trained on these simulations works on real photos with no fine-tuning as a general result, but the paper supports this only for the authors' own RAW photos and three ground-truth scenes.
The page says the ghost-reflection model assumes perfectly parallel panes and attributes that as a limitation, which the paper mentions only as a modeling assumption and not as an observed failure.
The page lists Egyptian tablet color improvement as a context finding, though the paper only gives this as a qualitative figure observation, not a measured result.

The claim that Generic super-resolution models (SUPIR, Real-ESRGAN) score below even the do nothing control on SSIM is unsupported: SUPIR SSIM_R is 56.8 and RESRGan SSIM_R 53.6, both below control 64.5, but SSIM_T of 64.6 and 65.6 is below control 86.3 while Bicubic SSIM_R beats control, so the blanket claim is only partly right.

The statement that Ours+rnd is significantly worse than the real context cites p<1.7e-11, but the paper attaches that p-value to the comparison of Ours versus Ours+rnd, so the attribution is questionable.
The phrase that the upsampler uses 29% fewer parameters than V-DESIRR appears only in a supplementary figure caption and is presented as a headline result, though it is supported.
candidate: The page says the lab's Fresnel value with kappa 1.5 gives about -4.6 stops at 0 degrees and -4.3 at 45 degrees, which is its own calculation and not in the paper.

The page says that removing only the linear (gamma-free) mixing is about as damaging as All+G, and reads the Table 1 Gamma row as +70 to +21, interpreting the ablation in a way the paper does not state.
The page gives a fixed formula for the 8-bit blend weight w equals alpha to the power 1/2.2 as a stand-in for prior methods, which is not from the paper.
The page claims DSRNet is worse than doing nothing on the clean layer in Figure 7, comparing 0.939 with 0.979, which the paper does not state.

The ablation text says removing only the linear gamma-free mixing is about as damaging as All+G (+70 to +21); the paper's Table 1 labels the gamma ablation as compressing t and r before compositing, so this is a slightly loose reading but is mostly supported.

The claim that the context photo helps because saturated sky colors are recovered, and that this leaves reflected cars or hurts the clean layer, goes a bit beyond the paper, which only says the authors believe this for specific examples.
